content.text:
# Video2Code: 3D Brick Studio

根据 `inputs/demo.mp4` 复刻录屏中的三维积木编辑网站，交付能在本地启动并实际操作的网页项目。主要需求来自视频的画面、指针动作和前后状态；本任务不提供原站源码。

## 交付

- 在分配的项目目录中创建完整代码和 `README.md`，写明启动命令。
- 使用 Node.js 22。提供 `npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000`；网站在 `/` 可访问。本次统一使用浏览器原生 JavaScript/HTML/CSS，预装 Three.js 0.180.0（import "three" 与 "three/addons/..."）。不提供 React/JSX 编译器。
- 资源放在本地。验收时禁止联网；不要使用录屏、截图、iframe 或原站来代替交互界面。
- 你需要实际启动、检查自己的网页，修复阻塞错误。最终答复给出入口、启动方式和已知未完成项；自述不代替验收。

## 复刻范围

1. 复现浅灰环境中的立体底板、积木、底部深色工具条、左侧模式按钮和清空对话框。保留视频中的主要比例、色彩、材质与反馈。
2. 实现视频展示的放置预览、网格吸附、相邻放置、在已有积木上叠放、颜色选择、宽/深选择及交换、播放/暂停展示模式、手动改变视角、擦除目标高亮和删除、清空确认。
3. 同一种操作应可重复，能作用于新位置和不同的已展示颜色/尺寸组合。转动视角、交换尺寸或删掉积木后，后续拾取、预览和搭建仍应正确。
4. 初次进入可采用视频开头的一块红色 2×2 积木，也可采用空底板。初始种子不计分；验收统一先清空再开始。
5. 清空对话框的 Cancel/关闭应保留模型，Clear 应移除全部积木并允许重新搭建。该取消语义是本题公开补充约定。
6. 清楚区分放置模式、手动视角模式和擦除模式。模式切换不能意外新增或删除积木。手动视角模式改变相机，不要求移动已放置的积木。

以下不在本版功能评分范围：未演示的文件打开/保存、撤销/重做、自定义颜色弹窗、声音、登录、云端协作、刷新后的作品持久化、手机触控、任意物理碰撞、悬空支撑规则或移动单块积木。界面上可保留其静态图标。不要为它们牺牲已展示的交互。

## 环境与预算

- 主模型最多 15 个逻辑请求轮次；每轮可以请求多个工具，所有调用分别计数。
- 最多 120 次工具调用。网关不执行输出 token 硬上限；每轮请求 9,000 仅为建议值，本轮硬预算是 15 轮调用及工具/图片次数。请简洁地推理并尽快通过工具实现和验证网页；实际 token 用量记录在报告中。
- 四个模型使用同一抽帧/浏览器工具，直接接收相同初始视频帧和后续请求的图片。初始 12 帧计入 256 帧预算。自己的网页截图也直接返回图片。
- 视频观察上限 256 帧；自己的网页观察上限 120 帧。缓存命中也计入逻辑预算。可按需精确抽帧，不限于初始缩略图。
- 视频长 41.333 秒，1280×804，30 fps；原音轨为全零静音，因此无需语音识别，不给音频理解分。
- 可运行、交互与状态一致性、视觉还原和基本可用性分别占 10、60、25、5 分。验收包含原顺序回放以及相同操作的不同位置/颜色/顺序组合；不增加未说明功能。

本题仅检验可观察结果，不限定内部数据结构、DOM 层级、CSS 类名或实现库。不要读取 evaluator/design 目录、原始 WebCompass checklist、其他候选结果或参考实现。

## 本次统一运行约束

项目从空白 index.html 开始。package.json、server.mjs 和 vendor/ 为只读可信环境；npm run dev 使用提供的静态服务器。只能编写前端文件和 README.md；不能执行任意宿主机 shell、Node 后端代码、读取评测目录或联网安装依赖。run_command 支持启动、语法检查和刷新。所有四模型使用完全相同的约束。可通过 browser_action 进行鼠标点击、拖动、键盘和截图来自检。

Initial sampled frames below. Each image is labelled with its reference timestamp. Your project initially contains only index.html, a fixed static server and package.json. Read/edit files using tools. The fixed server serves local /vendor/three/build/three.module.js and /vendor/three/examples/jsm/. Include the import map shown in initial index.html if importing bare three. You have 15 turns including this one; complete and test a working frontend.

summary.text:
Now I understand the app well. This looks like a Lego/brick builder app (similar to "Brick Studio"). Key details: - Baseplate ~20x20 studs, light lavender/gray, studded. Environment: light gray marble texture background. - Bottom toolbar (dark navy, rounded pill): undo, redo | 8 color circles (red/coral, orange, yellow, green, light blue, blue/indigo, purple, dark gray) | rainbow color wheel | width dropdown "2 ⌄" with tooltip "Width ([ smaller, ] bigger)", swap icon ⇆, depth dropdown "2 ⌄" | folder (open), save | play ▶, trash. - Left vertical buttons: hammer (Build, active when black), move/cross arrows (View mode), eraser (Erase). Tooltip "Erase (e)" etc. - Top-right: muted speaker icon and X. - Ghost preview: translucent yellow brick following pointer, snaps to grid, stacks on top of existing bricks. - Play mode: UI hidden, pause button (two vertical bars) centered at bottom, camera slowly rotates (at 18-20s the view angle is changing; likely auto-orbit). - View mode: user drags to orbit camera. - Erase mode: hover highlights brick (in 33.5s frame, purple brick at right appears lighter/highlighted — yes the right purple brick looks lighter lavender, indicating hover highlight), click deletes (at 33.5→35.5 the green brick on top-left was deleted? Comparing 32→33.5: a green brick disappeared from top and the purple highlight). At 35.5 eraser active again. - Clear dialog: dark overlay, white card, "Clear Set", text, Cancel (white, bordered) / Clear (red). X top right of card. Cancel keeps model; Clear empties. - Color selection: clicking color circles changes selected color (green selected at 3-13.5s, purple at 15+). - Width dropdown: popup with options 1-6, "3" highlighted on hover. Selected 3, then purple 3x2 placed at 16.5. Swap button at 23s swaps to 2x3. - Keyboard shortcuts: tooltips show "(e)", "(s)", "[ smaller, ] bigger" etc. Initial state: one red 2x2 brick already placed (frame 0). Allowed: initial seed not graded; evaluation starts by clearing. Toolbar also has undo/redo arrows (static ok). Open/save icons static. Now the plan: build with Three.js 0.180, OrbitControls from three/addons. Implement: Scene: - Background: light gray with subtle marble — could use a procedural canvas texture or just a radial gradient + noise. Simplest: CSS background on canvas container? The 3D environment includes a large ground plane beyond the baseplate (marble texture extends across the whole view). So scene has a big ground plane with marble texture (generated via canvas noise), plus fog maybe. Color ~ #d8d8de. - Lighting: hemisphere + directional with shadows. Shadows visible under bricks and studs. - Baseplate: 20x20 studs (looks like ~20x20 in the video; frame 0 count ~ 20 studs wide). Actually count: in frame 0, across the plate there seem to be ~20 studs. I'll go with 20x20. Plate is a box with stud cylinders on top. Use InstancedMesh for studs (400 instances). Plate color: light lavender #b9b9cf-ish... Looking at frame 0, the plate is light gray-lavender (#c2c2d4 maybe). Brick at 40s: plate appears white-ish. I'll pick #c6c6d8. Brick geometry: standard lego proportions: stud spacing 1 unit, brick height 1.2 units (lego: 8mm pitch, 9.6mm height → ratio 1.2). Stud radius 0.3, stud height 0.2. Build a BoxGeometry + stud cylinders, merged into one geometry per (w,d). Cache geometries. Material: MeshStandardMaterial (or MeshPhysical) with color, roughness ~0.35. Ghost preview: same geometry with transparent yellowish material (opacity 0.55, color pale yellow #e8e06a). Actually ghost appears pale yellow regardless of selected color. In video, ghost is always pale yellow. Yes — ghost color pale yellow with opacity. Placement logic: raycast against baseplate top and existing bricks. Determine target cell: if hitting plate, cell = floor coords; if hitting brick, stack on top (y = brick top), cell derived from hit point (slightly offset inward by face normal for side faces? In video, when hovering top of brick, preview stacks on top; hovering plate beside brick gives plate placement). Simplest: use hit point + normal*small offset, then compute grid cell: gx = round(point.x / stud) etc. Compute y = height of stack at that region: find max top among cells covered by the brick footprint. Standard approach: for candidate cell (cx, cz), compute base y = max over footprint cells of occupancy height. Place at that y if no overlap collision at that height. Occupancy: map from "x,z" cell to stack height / list of bricks. Collision: brick occupies cells at level [y, y+1). When placing at footprint, y = max height over footprint; ensure each cell's top <= y (no interpenetration). Snapping: width w along x, depth d along z. For even/odd dims, center alignment: cell center coordinates. Use grid where stud positions are at integer coords from -(N-1)/2..(N-1)/2. For a brick of size w×d, its min corner cell (i,j) → occupies i..i+w-1. Center = (i + (w-1)/2, j + (d-1)/2). Snap: compute i = round(hitX - (w-1)/2), j = round(hitZ - (d-1)/2). That keeps studs aligned. Clamp to plate bounds [0, N-w] etc. Erase mode: raycast bricks, hover → highlight (store original material, swap to lighter/emissive highlight). Click → remove brick, free cells. View mode: OrbitControls enabled; in other modes disabled? In video, in build mode the camera doesn't rotate on drag (probably). View mode button activates orbit. Play mode: UI hides, camera auto-rotates slowly, pause button bottom center; clicking pause exits back to edit mode (at 23s UI is back and camera at different angle — yes, exiting play keeps camera). Also drag in build mode with right button? Not required. Keep: orbit only in view mode (left drag rotate, wheel zoom). Also allow wheel zoom always? Not demonstrated; keep zoom only in view mode to avoid conflicts. Actually safer: enable OrbitControls zoom in all modes? The demo at 29s the camera zoomed out — that was after clicking view mode (button active at 29s: middle button black). Yes view mode active. So orbit controls only in view mode. Mode switching: buttons toggle active class (black = active, gray = inactive). Default: build mode active. Toolbar: - Undo/redo icons (static, grayed). - Colors: 8 swatches: #e74c3c-ish red/coral, orange #f0a04b, yellow #f7d354, green #58b368, light blue #63c5ea, blue #5b7fe0, purple #9b59d0, dark gray #4a4a52. Selected: white ring outline. - Rainbow wheel circle (custom color; can be static or opens nothing — out of scope; keep static icon, maybe a no-op or simple color input? "custom color popup" out of scope — keep static). - Width dropdown: button showing number + chevron; popup list 1-6 upward; tooltip "Width ([ smaller, ] bigger)". Keyboard [ ] adjusts width. - Swap button ⇆ swaps w/d; tooltip "Swap (s)"; key 's'. - Depth dropdown similar with tooltip probably "Depth". - Open/save icons static. - Play button ▶ → play mode. - Trash → clear dialog. Left buttons tooltips: Build (b)? In video we only saw "Erase (e)" tooltip. I'll add tooltips "Build (b)", "View (v)", "Erase (e)" with keys b/v/e. Top-right: speaker-x icon and X icon (static). Dialog: overlay rgba(0,0,0,0.6), card white rounded, "Clear Set" bold, message, Cancel (outlined pill), Clear (red pill #e05252), X close. Cancel/X keep model; Clear removes all bricks. Cursor: the pointer is purple-ish in the video (custom cursor?) — looks like a purple arrow cursor. That's likely just the recorder's cursor. Skip. Marble background: generate canvas texture: base #d9d9df with darker veins noise. Simple approach: fill with #dcdce2, add random translucent gray strokes/blotches. Good enough. Camera: initial position ~ (0, 14, 16) looking at origin, matching frame 0 view (plate seen from south, slightly above). FOV ~45. Play mode: hide toolbar/left buttons/top-right (fade out), show pause button bottom center; auto-rotate camera around target (azimuth += dt*speed). Click pause → exit play, restore UI. Erase highlight: on hover, set material emissive or lighten color: use mesh.material clone? Simpler: each brick mesh has userData.baseColor; on hover set material.color lerp toward white (e.g., color.clone().lerp(white, 0.5)) — at 33.5s the hovered purple brick looks lighter/desaturated lavender. So lighten by 0.45. On unhover restore. Ghost validity: if overlap (can't place), maybe hide ghost or show anyway. Keep simple: always compute placement; if collision detected at computed level... With max-height approach, collision only if a cell's stack is inside (top > y) — impossible since y = max top. So always placeable within bounds. Out of bounds → hide ghost. Bricks at different levels: brick height 1 level. Fine. Also ghost should not show in erase/view modes, and show only when pointer over plate/bricks. Shadow: directional light with shadow map, plate receives. Stud count 20: let me verify from frame 0: plate width in studs ~ count bumps: roughly 20. I'll use 20. Now check the plate proportion: in frame 0 the plate spans from x≈310 to x≈990 px (width 680) and depth from y≈180 to y≈770... it's perspective. Fine. Toolbar details: bg #171c2e-ish dark navy, pill, centered bottom, padding. Icons light gray #aab. Selected color has white 2px ring. Colors from video (approx): red #f25c54? The red brick is #c1272d-ish; swatch looks coral red #f26d5b. Bricks render darker due to lighting. Swatches: red(coral), orange, yellow, green, light blue, blue, purple, dark gray. I'll pick: #f2675c, #f5a623, #f7d54d, #6ec47b, #6fc7ee, #6f86e0, #b06fd8, #55555f. Ghost yellow: #e8e064 opacity 0.6. Width dropdown options 1-6 (video showed up to 6). Both dropdowns 1-6. Play button icon: triangle. Pause in play mode: "❚❚" two rounded bars. Keyboard: b/v/e modes, s swap, [ ] width? The width tooltip says "([ smaller, ] bigger)" meaning keys [ and ] adjust width. I'll implement [ ] for width, and maybe { }? For depth maybe ; '? Not shown. I'll do: [ ] width, - = depth? Not needed but harmless... Actually to be safe implement [ and ] for the currently... The tooltip at 13.5s says "Width ([ smaller, ] bigger)". For depth likely "Depth (; smaller, ' bigger)" — I'll guess , . for depth? Not graded likely. Implement [ ] width, ; ' depth. Undo/redo: out of scope — static buttons (could implement quickly with history stack... risk; keep static, title says out of scope). Now write the code. Single main.js module + index.html + styles.css + README.md. Implementation details: ```js import * as THREE from 'three'; import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'; import { mergeGeometries } from 'three/addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js'; ``` Scene setup: - renderer antialias, shadows PCFSoft, outputColorSpace default sRGB. - camera fov 45, pos (0, 15, 17), target (0,0,0). - lights: ambient/hemisphere (0xffffff, 0x8888aa, 0.9), directional (8, 14, 6) intensity 1.2, castShadow, shadow camera bounds ±16. - Ground: big plane 200x200 with marble canvas texture, receiveShadow. Position y = -0.36 (plate bottom). Plate: box 20*unit x 0.32 x 20*unit, top at y=0. Let's define: stud pitch P=1, plate top at y=0, plate box from -0.36 to 0 (thickness .36). Studs on plate: cylinders r=0.29, h=0.18, at integer coords -(N/2)+0.5? For N=20 even, stud positions x = i - 9.5 for i 0..19. Hmm center alignment: plate spans -10..10, studs at -9.5..9.5. Brick geometry(w,d): box w×1.2×d minus small clearance (0.96 factor? keep full size; fine), studs grid: x from -(w-1)/2 .. step 1, similarly z. Stud r .3 h .2 on top. Merge. Ghost: same geometry, material transparent yellow opacity 0.55, depthWrite false. Occupancy: `grid = new Map()` key `${i},${j}` → array of brick refs? Actually store per-cell stack: cells["i,j"] = [brickIds...]. brick = {i,j,w,d,y(level),mesh,id}. canPlace / stackTop(i,j) = number of bricks at cell (since each brick height 1, top level = count if contiguous; assume no floating — fine). place: compute level = max over footprint of cells height. Set brick y = level. Mesh position y = level*1.2 + 0.6 (center), plus plate top 0 and stud? Brick bottom sits at plate top y=0 (studs sink into plate visually). OK y_center = level*H + H/2 where H=1.2. Erase: remove brick, decrement cells, but bricks above would float — out of scope (floating allowed). But when removing a middle brick, cells' counts: cell stores list of {brick, level}. stackTop = max level+1. Compute as max over list. Good: store cell entries as array of brick objects with their base level. stackTop(i,j) = max(b.y+1) or 0. Raycast: intersect objects [plateTopMesh, ...brickMeshes]. Use hit point and face normal: - If hit plate: gx = point.x, gz = point.z. - If hit brick: use point + normal*0.01? For top face, point on top → we want cell above brick: compute gx from point.x anyway; level computed from footprint. For side faces, nudge point outward by normal*0.5 so the cell becomes adjacent. That gives "adjacent placement" when clicking sides. Video shows preview on top when hovering top; simple nudge works. i = Math.round(gx + 9.5 - (w-1)/2 - 0.5)? Let me define stud coord of cell i: x = i - 9.5, i in 0..19. Brick min corner cell i0: center x = i0 - 9.5 + (w-1)/2. So i0 = round(x + 9.5 - (w-1)/2). Similarly j0 = round(z + 9.5 - (d-1)/2). Clamp i0 to [0, 20-w], j0 to [0, 20-d]. If clamped too far from actual point (pointer outside plate), hide ghost? Just clamp; ghost near edge still shows — acceptable. Hover detection: raycast every pointermove; store hover target. Click behavior by mode: - build: place brick at ghost position with current color. - erase: if hover brick → delete. - view: orbit controls handle drag; click does nothing. Ensure mode switching doesn't add/delete: clicks on mode buttons are UI (canvas handler only on canvas). Also distinguish drag vs click in view mode — OrbitControls consumes drags; we don't place in view mode anyway. OrbitControls: enableDamping, minPolar 0.05, maxPolar ~1.45, minDistance 6, maxDistance 40. Enabled only in view mode (and play mode we auto-rotate by rotating controls manually: controls.autoRotate = true with autoRotateSpeed; controls.update()). In play mode set controls.enabled = false but autoRotate true and call update — autoRotate works when enabled=false? OrbitControls.update applies autoRotate regardless of enabled I believe (enabled only gates input listeners). Yes. Play mode UI: add class to body 'playing' → CSS hides .toolbar, .left-modes, .top-right; shows #pauseBtn. Pause click → exit. Camera initial: match frame 0 — plate viewed from front-ish, slight elevation. Position (0, 14, 18). Now UI layout numbers: toolbar bottom ~28px, centered, height ~52px, border-radius 26px, bg #181d2e, gap groups separated by thin dividers (rgba white .15). Left buttons: 44px circles at left 28px, top 28/90/152, bg: active #0d0f18, inactive rgba(255,255,255,0.35) with white icons... In video inactive buttons look semi-transparent white/gray circles with dark-ish icons? Frame 0: hammer black circle white icon (active); other two: light gray translucent circles with white icons. Tooltips: dark pill with white text. Dialog: as described. Dropdown popup: white rounded card, options 1-6, hover bg #f0f0f5, current maybe bold/highlighted. Opens upward above the button. Click outside closes. Tooltip implementation: data-tip attribute + CSS ::after? Position above element. For dropdowns the tooltip appeared above toolbar ("Width ([ smaller, ] bigger)"). Use CSS ::after with content attr(data-tip), show on hover. Swap icon: use ⇆ char or SVG. I'll use simple SVGs/unicode: undo ↺ redo ↻ (actually arrows: "↩"/"↪"), swap "⇆", folder 📁? Use inline SVG minimal paths to look decent. Unicode chars render inconsistently; but fine for prototype. I'll use text glyphs: ⟲ ⟳ for undo/redo, ⌄ chevron, ▶ play, 🗑 trash (emoji colored red in video; use SVG trash), folder and save as SVG simple. I'll craft small inline SVGs for: hammer, move, eraser, undo, redo, swap, folder, save, play, trash, volume-x, close. Keep simple strokes. Colors in video for brick materials: red brick #c1272d, green #2e8b3a, purple #7b2fbf. Ghost yellow. Swatch → brick color mapping: same hex, lighting will darken. Selected swatch ring: box-shadow 0 0 0 2px #181d2e, 0 0 0 4px #fff? In video white ring directly around circle with slight gap: box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #181d2e (gap matching bg), 0 0 0 4px white. Erase highlight: lighten color by 40% toward white and slight emissive. Also hover on swatches etc cursor pointer. Prevent text selection. Grid/plate edge: plate slightly transparent? It looks solid light lavender. Use color #c7c7da, roughness 0.6. Studs same color slightly lighter? Same material. Ground marble texture canvas 512: fill #dadae0; draw ~40 random translucent gray arcs/lines veins; also large soft blotches. Apply with slight repeat. Also add scene.fog? The background beyond ground in video is same marble to edges; ground plane 300 size with camera maxDistance 40 fine. Background color same as ground base so horizon blends. Shadow under plate edges: directional light shadow camera cover ±16. Extra: bricks cast+receive shadows; plate receives. Ghost must also show stacked on brick tops: when hovering a brick top, point on top face; i0 computed from x/z; level = max stack over footprint → 1 → ghost at level1. Edge case: hovering brick side face → nudge out by 0.5 along normal gives adjacent cell on plate level 0. Good. Raycast targets: plate box mesh + brick meshes list. Ghost excluded. Erase mode cursor highlight only when hovering brick. Placement sound none. Also disable ghost while dialog open or play mode. Write files now. Then serve + screenshot test + interactions. Note camera aspect: renderer full window. Let me also add "initial red 2×2 brick" at center-left as in frame 0 (cell around center). Place red 2x2 at i0=8? Center cells: x -0.5..0.5. Video: red brick slightly left of center. i0=8,j0=9 (cells 8-9, 9-10 → centered x=-0.5,z=0.5). Fine — seed not graded. Undo/redo static: disabled style (dim). In video they appear normal color but never used. Keep slightly dimmed, no action. The rainbow wheel: conic-gradient circle. Depth tooltip text: "Depth (, smaller, . bigger)"? I'll write "Depth". Keys: implement [ ] width, , . depth, s swap, b/v/e modes, p play? fine. Toolbar structure: ```
| folder save | play trash
``` Dropdown popups appended to toolbar positioned above respective button. Now write the code. For the pause button in play mode: white/translucent "❚❚" — in video it's white bars on transparent. Make two white rounded bars, semi-transparent. Pointer events: canvas listens pointermove/pointerdown. Distinguish click vs drag for placement: only place on pointerdown? Video: single clicks place. Use 'click' on renderer dom but ignore if drag distance > few px (view mode only anyway). In build mode no orbit, so click fine. One more: ghost should update continuously as pointer moves (raycast on pointermove) — yes. Write files.
